topic: Quantum Superposition and the Mystery of States

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Classical Binary
lecture_lines: A light switch is either 'On' or 'Off'.
Objects exist in definite states daily.
animations: Create two text blocks '0' and '1' in #FFFFFF.
Toggle a switch graphic from OFF state to ON state in #FFFF00.
Highlight '0' and '1' to emphasize definite state existence in #00FF00.

sections.title: Defining Superposition
lecture_lines: A qubit can be in two states simultaneously.
Superposition is like playing a chord.
animations: Display |0> and |1> states fading in together in #FFFFFF.
Draw the equation |ψ⟩ = α|0⟩ + β|1⟩ in #FFFFFF.
Animate the transition of a single point oscillating between |0> and |1> in #FF00FF.
Layer both states over each other to form a blur in #00FFFF.
Snap the blurred state into a clear |0> or |1> upon 'measurement' in #FFFFFF.

sections.title: The Measurement Problem
lecture_lines: The probability wave sharpens into one point.
Interaction with measurement forces a classical reality.
Schrödinger’s Cat is a cloud of states.
Opening the box forces a choice.
animations: Draw a wave function icon in #FFFFFF transforming into a single dot.
Show a probability distribution bell curve flattening into a spike in #FFFF00.
Illustrate a measurement probe hitting the state in #FF0000.
Fade in a box icon containing a blurry cat state in #FFFFFF.
Snap the box open to reveal only a single state in #FFFFFF.

sections.title: Visualizing the Probability Cloud
lecture_lines: Coefficients α and β represent probabilities.
animations: Animate the sum icon constant as α and β values adjust in #00FF00.
Display a die spinning with changing face values in #FFFF00.

sections.title: Application: Quantum Computing
lecture_lines: Classical bits test paths one by one.
Quantum computers process all paths simultaneously.
animations: Draw a set of paths in #FFFFFF diverging from a source.
Highlight single bits iterating through each path slowly in #FF0000.
Simultaneously light up all paths in #00FF00 to show quantum parallelism.
